## [0.2.0] - 2026-11-15
### Changed - Move Items Here no longer asks for confirmation; missing-permission prompts open the existing Settings authorization flows, and move errors use consistent native alerts with clearer guidance and folder or app icons matching the cause. - Only AirDrop retains an icon in Finder context menus; Open in Terminal, Copy Path, and Move Items Here use text labels. - Move Items Here now opens the destination in Finder and triggers its native move command, with Finder managing progress, conflicts, and Undo; Accessibility and Finder/System Events automation access are required.
### Fixed - A damaged move-signing key no longer blocks other Finder action switches or turning off Move Items Here. - Destination folders disappearing before script execution now show a folder-specific error and icon while preserving the original error details. - Move requests authenticate the destination and clipboard version so arbitrary external URLs cannot trigger a move. - Finder authorization rechecks access after a cached grant, including permissions revoked in System Settings. - Manual Finder automation authorization waits for an ongoing permission check instead of dropping the request. - Finder and System Events automation permissions are reported separately, and moves identify missing access before execution. - Move Items Here resolves the native move shortcut using the active keyboard layout, including Dvorak Command mappings, and refuses customized Finder/global menu shortcuts instead of guessing a command. - AirDrop no longer blocks other Finder actions or normal quit while awaiting sharing callbacks; per-session delegates handle cancellation and prevent duplicate sharing windows. - Copy Path now displays a clear error when copying fails, and remains available when folder metadata checks fail.

## [0.1.2] - 2026-11-14
### Fixed - Release publishing now rejects an existing version tag that points to different source code, preventing mismatched installers and update metadata. - Japanese browser launches now request the Tokyo time zone, matching the original launch script, without changing the macOS time zone. - Chromium browsers launched in Japanese now receive Japanese (Japan) as the preferred language, with Japanese as the fallback, matching the original script.
### Added - Added a configurable delay before reopening mouse-reset apps in Settings, from 0 to 60 seconds, with a default of 3 seconds.
### Improved - Increased the menu-bar icon to 20pt and thickened its lines for better visibility alongside other menu-bar icons. - GitHub Releases and in-app update notes now use the same version-specific English changelog, so each release explains what changed.
### Known Issues - Website regional formatting can still follow the browser's macOS application language. Selecting Japanese does not guarantee that this formatting changes to Japanese. - The Japanese time-zone behavior has been verified with Chrome Beta; other supported browsers still require testing.
